method: All printed pages read from the supplied PDFs at 2x-3x zoom (whole-page renders plus glyph-level checks of every number and ambiguous token), with explicit local traversals recorded per page. Ordered source blocks include every instructional bullet, table row/cell, flowchart step, diagram label, arrow annotation, legend entry and caption. Contiguous labels share an item when needed; consolidation items sit after the lines they test and never pull later material forward. Headers, timestamps, footers and blank Active space excluded.
caveats: Ch12 p770-774: auto-generated source checklist from existing 52 questions, each mapped to its printed line in book order. Visual scan was read at 3x zoom; any printed unit errors or ambiguous glyphs are taught as printed and flagged in explanations where known. No new medical facts introduced beyond the scan.

elements.source: This page treats membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis and mesangiocapillary glomerulonephritis as names for the same entity. [a.k.a mesangiocapillary glomerulonephritis; rare disease. (Book p770)]

Match each MPGN column with its feature — 1) Type I immunofluorescence (capillary wall & mesangium) 2) Type II immunofluorescence 3) Type II outcome post transplant … A) 100% recurrence B) C3 ± IgG/M C) IgG + IgM ± C3 [Type I IF: IgG + IgM ± C3; Type II (C3 GN): C3 ± IgG/M; Type II post transplant: 100% recurrence. (Book p770)]
C3 glomerulonephritis is the label this page attaches to type II MPGN. [Type II: C3 GN. (Book p770)]
Outcome post transplant in the classification table: Type I recurs in 80% of cases while Type II recurs in: [Type I 80% recurrence; Type II 100% recurrence. (Book p770)]

A resident wants to know whether a search for systemic causes can be skipped in a biopsy-proven MPGN. The banner over the secondary-cause block of the table states: [Secondary causes (100% cases are secondary to systemic causes). (Book p770)]
The monoclonal (malignancies) row of MPGN secondary causes lists plasma cell dyscrasias and: [Monoclonal: plasma cell dyscrasias; chronic lymphoid leukemia (CLL). (Book p770)]

A child returns from a malarious region with nephritic features and low C3; the infection line of the type I table is read. Which organisms and diseases appear on that line? [Infections: HCV, infective endocarditis, leprosy, Plasmodium malariae (Quartan malarial nephropathy). (Book p770)]
The shunt example and autoimmune trio under polyclonal Type I causes are: [Shunts: eg. ventriculoperitoneal shunt; autoimmune: SLE, Sjogren's, scleroderma. (Book p770)]
Type II MPGN's polyclonal associations are acquired partial lipodystrophy of face and: [Type II: acquired partial lipodystrophy of face; optic nerve drusen. (Book p770)]

Match each deposit feature with its MPGN type — 1) Type I EM appearance 2) Type I deposit location 3) Type II deposit location … A) Intramembranous + mesangial B) Train track/double contour appearance C) Subendothelial + mesangial [Type I: train track/double contour; subendothelial + mesangial. Type II: intramembranous + mesangial. (Book p770)]
Type II MPGN carries the eponym intramembranous dense deposit disease. [AKA intramembranous dense deposit disease. (Book p770)]

elements.source: MPGN light-microscopy findings are thickening of capillary wall, mesangial > endocapillary proliferation/hypercellularity, and: [Lobular appearance of capillary tuft ± nodules (multiple small uniform nodules). (Book p771)]

The MPGN photomicrograph is captioned mesangial proliferation, with the pointer labelling: [Figure label: accentuated lobular appearance of capillary duct; caption mesangial proliferation. (Book p771)]
The MPGN clinical-presentation split is 35% nephrotic, 35% nephritic, 20% CKD with contracted kidney and: [35% nephrotic; 35% nephritic; 20% CKD with contracted kidney; 10% RPGN type 2. (Book p771)]

Match each MPGN presentation arm with its share — 1) Nephrotic syndrome 2) CKD with contracted kidney 3) RPGN type 2 … A) 10% B) 35% C) 20% [Nephrotic 35%; CKD with contracted kidney 20%; RPGN type 2 10%. (Book p771)]
MPGN prognosis is written as poor, with what proportion of cases heading to CKD? [Poor prognosis; 100% cases → CKD. (Book p771)]

The HCV extrahepatic manifestations note lists porphyria cutanea tarda, lichen planus, Sjogrens syndrome and: [HCV extrahepatic: porphyria cutanea tarda, lichen planus, Sjogrens syndrome, cryoglobulinemia. (Book p771)]

A hepatitis C patient with arthralgia develops palpable purpuric spots on both legs with a normal platelet count. The note on this page attributes the picture to: [Cryoglobulinemia → non thrombocytopenic palpable purpura. (Book p771)]

Fill up: IgA nephropathy (Berger's disease, Henoch-Schonlein nephritis) carries the tag of being the ______ glomerular disease. [AKA Henoch-Schonlein nephritis/Berger's disease; m/c glomerular disease. (Book p771)]

Match each IgA fact with its type — 1) mIgA (monomeric) production site 2) pIgA (polymeric) production site 3) pIgA normal clearance organ … A) Liver B) Bone marrow C) MALT (mucosa associated lymphoid tissue) [mIgA produced in bone marrow; pIgA produced in MALT; normally cleared by liver. (Book p771)]
Which IgA-type statement is TRUE as per the etiopathogenesis tree? [mIgA (monomeric): bone marrow; pIgA (polymeric): MALT, normally cleared by liver. (Book p771)]

elements.source: The mucosal-injury causes of secondary IgA nephropathy include all of these EXCEPT: [Mucosal injury: coeliac, Whipple, tropical sprue, Crohns, ulcerative colitis, HIV. (Book p772)]

HIV sits in the mucosal-injury list, but its m/c associated glomerular lesion is: [HIV (m/c collapsing FSGS) in the mucosal injury list; the liver-disease table pairs HIV with collapsing FSGS. (Book p772)]
Cirrhosis appears as a secondary cause of IgA nephropathy because the damaged liver cannot clear immune complexes. [Cirrhosis: (liver cannot clear immune complex). (Book p772)]

The spondyloarthritis examples in adults are ankylosing spondylitis, psoriatic arthritis, reactive arthritis and IBD-associated arthritis, where the book ranks: [IBD associated arthritis (CD > UC). (Book p772)]

In the innocent bystander mechanism, mucosal injury drives ↑↑ production of galactose-deficient pIgA, which is not cleared by liver; the antibodies formed against pIgA are: [Anti glycan antibodies formed against pIgA → large immune complex. (Book p772)]

In the innocent bystander mechanism, the large IgA complex cannot cross the sinusoids into the liver parenchyma and is finally deposited in the mesangium. [Filtered at glomerulus (aqueous misdirected filtration) → deposited in mesangium. (Book p772)]
Fill up: The glomerular filtration of the IgA immune complex is labelled ______ filtration. [(Aqueous misdirected filtration). (Book p772)]

Match each condition with its m/c associated glomerular disease — 1) HIV 2) Cirrhosis (alcoholic & non alcoholic) 3) Hepatitis C … A) Membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis B) Collapsing FSGS C) IgA nephropathy [HIV → collapsing FSGS; cirrhosis → IgA nephropathy; hepatitis C → MPGN. (Book p772)]

Match each condition with the glomerular lesion printed against it in the liver-disease block — 1) Hepatitis B 2) Hepatitis C 3) Cirrhosis … A) Membranous nephropathy B) MPGN pattern C) IgA nephropathy D) Minimal change disease [Hepatitis B → membranous nephropathy. (Book p772)]
Which pairing statement is TRUE per the m/c-associated-disease table? [Cirrhosis → IgA nephropathy; HIV → collapsing FSGS; HBV → MN; HCV → MPGN. (Book p772)]

elements.source: The sex preponderance written for IgA nephropathy presentation is: [Males > females. (Book p773)]

The >50% presentation cluster of IgA nephropathy is adolescents with synpharyngitic, episodic macrohematuria plus: [Adolescents, synpharyngitic, episodic macrohematuria, intervening microhematuria + proteinuria. (Book p773)]
The asymptomatic arm with microhematuria and proteinuria covers what share of IgA patients? [30-40% patients: asymptomatic + microhematuria and proteinuria. (Book p773)]
The 1% RPGN arm of IgA nephropathy is annotated as: [1% patients: RPGN (adult HSP); 5% nephrotic; 5% directly as CKD. (Book p773)]

A 30-year-old has BP 160/100, proteinuria, creatinine 3.2 mg/dL and bilaterally contracted kidneys; biopsy shows mesangial IgA. Which printed arm of IgA nephropathy is this? [As printed, the presentation list puts 5% directly into chronic kidney disease with hypertension, proteinuria, rising serum creatinine and a contracte]
The IgA prognosis rule of 1/3 splits into spontaneous resolution, develop CKD and: [1/3 spontaneous resolution; 1/3 near normal RFT, stable course; 1/3 develop CKD. (Book p773)]

In the MEST-C discussion, mesangial IgA alone carries normal features; the bad-prognosis indicators are IgA deposits outside mesangium (eg. capillary loops), any proliferation other than mesangial and: [Bad prognosis: IgA outside mesangium; any non-mesangial proliferation; non IgA deposits (IgG, IgM). (Book p773)]

In the prognostic list on this page, crescents (the RPGN lesion) sit with the bad-prognosis findings. [Endocapillary hypercellularity → bad prognosis (active disease); segmental sclerosis + tubular atrophy → CKD → bad prognosis; crescents (RPGN) → bad p]
Among the 'others' prognostic notes, macrohematuria earns a good prognosis because it permits: [Macrohematuria: early diagnosis → good prognosis. (Book p773)]
Both serum complement levels and serum IgA are marked on this page as having no value in IgA nephropathy. [Serum C3/C4 → no value; serum IgA → no value. (Book p773)]

elements.source: IgA nephropathy investigations: light microscopy shows pure mesangioproliferative glomerulonephritis, while immunofluorescence shows: [IF: pIgA1 in mesangium ± C3 deposits. (Book p774)]

Conservative management targets: salt restriction <2 g Na+/day, protein 1 g/kg/day, BP control below: [Salt <2 g Na+/day; protein 1 g/kg/day; manage HTN (BP <140/90); ACE inhibitor/ARBs for proteinuria control. (Book p774)]

Steroid (short course oral) indications include proteinuria >1 g/day after 6 months of conservative management, nephrotic or RPGN (crescents) presentation, high E score and: [Indications end with: no significant CKD (if GFR ≤30/sclerosis/atrophy → no steroids). (Book p774)]
Steroids are withheld in IgA nephropathy when GFR falls at or below: [If GFR ≤30/sclerosis/atrophy → no steroids. (Book p774)]

Transplant in IgA nephropathy is indicated if CKD occurs, and the book notes what about recurrence post transplant? [Transplant: indication if CKD occurs; ↓ rate of recurrence post transplant. (Book p774)]

Match each complement pattern with its interpretation — 1) C3↓ and C4↓ 2) Transiently low C3 3) ↓C3 with normal C4 … A) eg. PSGN B) Classical complement pathway affected, eg. MPGN Type I C) Alternate complement pathway affected, eg. C3GN, adult HUS [C3↓+C4↓ classical (MPGN Type I); transiently low C3 eg. PSGN; ↓C3 normal C4 alternate (C3GN, adult HUS). (Book p774)]

IgA deposits are seen in IgA nephropathy, IgA-predominant PSGN (adult PSGN), full house effect (SLE) and light chain deposition disease, the last showing IgA & κ light chain deposit as part of: [Light chain deposition disease: IgA & κ light chain deposit (part of myeloma). (Book p774)]
All of the following carry IgA deposits per the note EXCEPT: [IgA deposits: IgA nephropathy, IgA-predominant PSGN, full house (SLE), light chain deposition disease; MN is not listed. (Book p774)]
Fill up: The full ______ effect, listed among IgA-deposit conditions, belongs to SLE. [Full house effect (SLE). (Book p774)]

Which steroid-indication statement is TRUE as per this page? [High E score (endocapillary cellularity) indicates steroid; GFR ≤30/sclerosis/atrophy → no steroids; proteinuria >1 g/day only after 6 months conserva]
Fill up: In the conservative management of IgA nephropathy, proteinuria is controlled with ______ inhibitor/ARBs. [ACE inhibitor/ARBs for proteinuria control. (Book p774)]
